subject.title: [Bug]: Discord routing / mention-gating issue in OpenClaw

question: Should Discord preflight adopt strict active-target scoping that suppresses the current/default agent when another configured agent, role target, or quoted/later mention signal means the current agent is not being addressed?
rationale: The source gap is concrete, but the fix changes stable Discord routing precedence, role semantics, and bot-loop behavior for multi-agent guild setups.

options.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
options.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages targeting other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and require live Discord proof.

options.title: Split narrower contracts
options.body: Keep this issue open as coordination while the narrower role-trigger, reply/default-owner, slash-command, and bot-authored reply items settle their own contracts.

options.title: Keep current default-owner behavior
options.body: Document the current routing and ignoreOtherMentions behavior as the contract, then close follow-ups that conflict with it.

recommendation.title: Adopt strict active-target scoping
recommendation.body: Implement Discord-owned target resolution before default routing, drop messages targeting other configured agents, scope mention text to the opening attention window, and require live Discord proof.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest history on the shared mention policy and Discord routing extraction that this decision would change.
